_note: Numbers taken off the desk's BofA Hindalco model (13006375.xlsx, supplied
2026-08-25; Bharat Subramanian, bharat.subramanian@bofa.com). 11 sheets.
THESE ARE MODEL VALUES, NOT PRINTS. factor='estimate' on every forecast row
so nothing here can resolve as an observation of fact. The FY26 rows are the
model's view of a completed year, which is still the model's view - where the
company published the same quantity, the company's figure is what the specs
use (base_financials.yaml precedence: a company release beats the model).
WHY THE CONVERSION SPREAD MATTERS. `can_sheet_spread` has no public series -
not from the company, not from any free feed, not on the Daily Metals Pack.
The model's 'Premium (US$/t)' over LME is the only quantification of it
anywhere available to this system, which is why it is captured even though it
is an annual model value rather than a price.
AND WHY THE SCRAP LEG IS DEAD. Every sheet was searched for a scrap price.
The only scrap rows in the workbook are 'Recycled content' (a percentage) and
an EBITDA-level '- Elimination/scrap benefit' in US$mn. The model prices
Novelis' raw material AT LME. So `al_scrap_midwest` is now unsourced in three
independent places - company disclosure, free market data, and the sell-side
model. That is a settled negative, not a gap to keep waiting on.
THE DEFINITION TRAP, recorded so nobody 'fixes' the spec to the model. The
model's Novelis FY26 Adj. EBITDA is $2,057mn against the company's reported
$1,645mn on IDENTICAL shipments of 3,557 kt. Row 87 of the Novelis sheet is
'- Elimination/scrap benefit' = $411mn, and 2,057 - 1,645 = 412. Different
EBITDA definition, reconciled to within $1mn. novelis.base_ebitda uses the
company's figure and must keep doing so.
